query:
The group regularly does a shared meal before dark-sky sessions — Cecilia organises these and they seem like part of the tradition. Does this actually apply to all members? If not, who opts out and how does the chat show this?

Options:
A. Jerome
B. Tomás
C. Ruth
D. Marcus
context:
[1] (about=Cecilia, episodic, t2 @2026-02-06T20:36:00) ok back to Feb 17th logistics, do we want to do the group meal first or go straight to site? I was thinking Thai takeaway at mine at 6:30 then car share to Blackmoor by 8? 🍜🌟
[2] (about=Ruth, episodic, t4 @2026-03-06T20:10:00) Is it possible that we compromise, perhaps one deeper-dark-sky session per season for those who want it, with Blackmoor remaining the default? That way nobody is left out on the regular outings.
[3] (about=Harriet, episodic, t14 @2026-08-07T20:38:00) Looking back at this year: Jerome on nebulae, Tomás on a proper mount, Ruth converted to dark sites, Cecilia blending Ha. Nadia and Ruth still the constants at the centre of it all. I think this group has had its best year yet and I am going to make sure the podcast reflects that. How would you each describe what this summer gave you that you did not have in January?
[4] (about=Harriet, episodic, t10 @2026-06-05T20:49:00) Unanimous then, or nearly. I will note for the record that I pushed for darker sites before the weekend and I am gratified. But I want to add something: this group started in Nadia's back garden, did it not? Nadia, Ruth, you two dragged everyone here. I think people forget that the whole thing was your idea originally.
[5] (about=Cecilia, episodic, t14 @2026-08-07T20:29:00) I came to a public star party three years ago expecting to be bored and left having already signed up for the next session. I think most people here have a version of that story. One look at something real through an eyepiece and that's it, you're done. I am organising the annual dark-sky weekend again for next October and I would love for Harriet to record the whole event for the podcast!!! 🌟🌟🌟
[6] (about=Nadia, episodic, t14 @2026-08-07T20:22:00) Ruth and I met at the county natural-history society in 2021 and discovered within about twenty minutes that we both preferred the stars to anything else on the programme. We agreed to meet the following Friday with our own telescopes in my back garden. There were two of us, a 4-inch refractor, Ruth's old 80mm, and a thermos of tea. I remember we stayed out until 2am on a school night and neither of us could see the point of going in. It grew from there one person at a time. In my experience the quiet beginning is the only honest beginning a group like this can have.
[7] (about=Ruth, episodic, t10 @2026-06-05T20:44:00) In favour. Though I would note that for a pure double-star session on a steady night, Blackmoor is still adequate. Seeing matters more than darkness for splitting tight pairs.
[8] (about=Ruth, episodic, t12 @2026-07-10T20:37:00) I cannot speak to the technical aspects but the image looks beautiful. Is it possible that what you have both done this evening is exactly the kind of collaboration that makes this group worth belonging to?
[9] (about=Nadia, episodic, t10 @2026-06-05T20:26:00) Ruth, that is perhaps the most gratifying thing I have heard in five years of this group. In my experience it takes one genuinely dark night to make the argument permanently. I am delighted the weekend did that for you.
[10] (about=Harriet, episodic, t8 @2026-05-08T20:40:00) I want to do an episode built around that weekend. The group, the dark sky, the contrast between people seeing it for the first time and veterans like Nadia who have been chasing this for thirty years. Dev, your reaction on the night would be perfect audio.
[11] (about=Cecilia, core, t8 @2026-05-08T20:16:00) Cecilia agreed to organise a proper dark-sky weekend trip this summer, suggesting a two-hour drive with accommodation.
[12] (about=Cecilia, core, t14 @2026-08-07T20:11:00) Cecilia came to a public star party three years ago expecting to be bored and left having signed up for the next session; she is organising the annual dark-sky weekend again for next October and wants Harriet to record the whole event for the podcast.
[13] (about=Jerome, episodic, t2 @2026-02-06T20:38:00) I will go straight to site. I need to be set up and aligned by 7:45 to make the most of the window. dinner beforehand doesn't work with my acquisition schedule.
[14] (about=Marcus, episodic, t10 @2026-06-05T20:38:00) dev and I stayed up till 3am watching jupiter and saturn transit. the seeing came up to 4/5 around 1am and at 400x on jupiter you could see three festoons in the NEB simultaneously. that's the best planetary night I've had in two years
[15] (about=Nadia, episodic, t8 @2026-05-08T20:31:00) I have been saying this since session one. In my experience there is no substitute for genuine darkness. The Milky Way shadow phenomenon happens around SQM 22.0 or above. You cannot replicate it closer to town, full stop.
[16] (about=Ruth, said_by=Harriet, profile, t10 @2026-06-05T20:23:00) Harriet noted Ruth said on Saturday night that she had been recommending books about dark skies for years but had never actually experienced one; Harriet wants to use it as the episode's opening line.
[17] (about=Ruth, core, t4 @2026-03-06T19:49:00) Ruth proposes a compromise of one deeper-dark-sky session per season for those who want it, with Blackmoor remaining the default.
agent_answer:
**A. Jerome**

Cecilia proposes the shared meal (Thai takeaway at 6:30, then car share to Blackmoor), and she is the one who keeps organising the group's dark-sky logistics. But the chat shows it does not apply to everyone: **Jerome** explicitly opts out.

His own words in the memory slice:

> "I will go straight to site. I need to be set up and aligned by 7:45 to make the most of the window. dinner beforehand doesn't work with my acquisition schedule."

So the pre-session meal is a Cecilia-led tradition that Jerome declines — driven by his imaging/acquisition schedule rather than any dispute.

(The records for Dev, Priya and Tomás are silent on the meal, so they neither confirm nor opt out; Ruth and Marcus show no such refusal.)
